introduction: On this second Sunday of Easter, Divine Mercy Sunday, the risen Jesus comes through locked doors, gives his disciples peace and breathes on them the Holy Spirit for the forgiveness of sins. Thomas doubts, then confesses, My Lord and my God. In the second reading, the risen Christ tells John, Do not be afraid; I am the first and the last, the living one. Let us receive the mercy of the risen Lord.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the risen Lord stands among us and says, Peace be to you. Let us pray to the Father of mercies.
intentions: For the Church: that she may be a sign of the mercy and peace of the risen Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For priests who hear confessions: that they may be faithful ministers of God's forgiveness. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the sick and all who are suffering in body or mind: that the risen Lord may heal and strengthen them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who doubt: that they may meet the risen Lord, as Thomas did. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may be merciful as our heavenly Father is merciful. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God of mercy, your Son rose from the dead and gave the Spirit for the forgiveness of sins. Make us witnesses of your mercy, and keep us in the peace of the risen Lord. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: I am the living one
reflection.body:
On the evening of the first Easter, the disciples are locked in, afraid. Jesus comes and stands among them: "Peace be to you." He shows them his wounds, and "The disciples therefore were glad when they saw the Lord." Then he breathes on them: "Receive the Holy Spirit! If you forgive anyone's sins, they have been forgiven them." The risen Lord's first gift is forgiveness, which is why this Sunday, since Saint John Paul II established it in 2000, is also called Divine Mercy Sunday.

Thomas was absent and refuses to believe. A week later Jesus comes again and invites him to touch his wounds. Thomas answers with the greatest confession of faith in the Gospels: "My Lord and my God!" And Jesus speaks to all of us who come after: "Blessed are those who have not seen and have believed."

The first reading shows the power of the risen Lord at work through the apostles. "By the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were done among the people." People even laid the sick in the streets so that Peter's shadow might fall on them.

In the Book of Revelation, John is in exile on the island of Patmos, "on the Lord's day," when he sees the risen Christ in glory. He falls down as though dead, but Christ lays his hand on him and says, "Don't be afraid. I am the first and the last, and the Living one. I was dead, and behold, I am alive forever and ever." And he adds, "I have the keys of Death and of Hades."

The wounds Jesus shows are not erased by the Resurrection. They have become signs of his love. This week, bring your fears and wounds to the risen Lord. If you can, go to confession and receive his mercy. And say to him with Thomas: My Lord and my God.
